validation.notes: Single command from the workspace root; 9 cross-module observations pass. Repaired files: (1) packages/agent/src/harness/runtime/drive/tools.ts recoverToolInvocation now requires both declarations before replay (call.replay === "safe" && tool !== undefined && tool.replay === "safe"), so stored-safe/current-never, stored-never/current-safe and missing-tool recoveries stay interrupted, keep the durable checkpoint, read it, and publish the interruption marker instead of executing; (2) packages/agent/src/harness/execution/effect-gate.ts gate.admit now performs the existing synchronous check() before invoke(), so an aborting gate throws AbortRequested(cancellation) and a closed gate rethrows its closing error without running the admitted work; (3) packages/agent/src/harness/execution/tools.ts executeToolCall now passes call.args (cleared/persisted arguments) to tool.execute instead of call.toolCall.arguments, while the provider tool call object stays unchanged. The regression script loads the real submitted drive/execution/gate modules through .prale-eval/subject.mjs (only checkpoint storage, progress transport, hook delivery and the tool effect boundary are faked). It asserts: checkpoint clear precedes the replay invocation; safe replay executes exactly the persisted arguments once and publishes isError:false with the tool result; publication happens only after a promise-controlled progress drain completes and live updates/checkpoint writes are delivered; unsafe or missing declarations never cross the effect boundary and never clear the checkpoint; durable cancellation and an aborting gate refuse admission entirely; a closed gate rejects the pass with its closing error and publishes nothing. Faulty-baseline detection was verified locally by restoring each production file alone to its pre-repair content (gate admission skipping state, executor using call.toolCall.arguments, replay condition using || ): each restoration makes the script fail with an explicit node:assert/strict AssertionError (not an import error, crash or timeout), and the repaired tree passes again. Asynchronous ordering uses only promises (deferred drain + microtask flushing); no timers, randomness, network, credentials or external services are used. The script creates its workspace-local scratch input under .prale-eval/.tmp-regression-scratch/ and removes it in a finally block. Limitation recorded: the repository vitest suites were not executed because node_modules is absent and installing dependencies is out of scope; the Node 24 standalone regression above is the executed validation.
